Each task must deliver a distinct succint outcome/value increment, and be so easy to implement that a dumb junior llm agent could implement it flawlessly in max 2-4 hours. There must be a prompt attached to eact task so that a human can provide the instructions manually if needed.

<skill_content name="brainstorming">
# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

# Agentic ODI [![Open the Living Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20the%20Living%20Studio-F38020?style=for-the-badge&logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/) [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, the CLI tree, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, conversation history, and the PM memory store, plus the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders, evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails

This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.

> **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.

---

## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails

This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.

### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?

ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.

ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.

---

### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done

- A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
- A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
- **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
- ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.

---

### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes

- **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
- Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
- **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):

  > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`

  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.

- **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.

---

### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)

- All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
  1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
  2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
  3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
  4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
  5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
  6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
  7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
  8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs

- **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
- ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.

---

### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)

- Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
  - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
  - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?

- **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):

  ```
  Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
  ```

- **Interpretation**:
  - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
  - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
  - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.

- **Agent rule**: Always compute and surface the opportunity score when both `importance` and `satisfaction` are provided. Highlight outcomes scoring **> 10** as the highest priority innovation targets. Use `get_outcomes(job_id)` to review the full opportunity landscape.

---

### Stage 5: Outcome-Based Market Segmentation

- ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation (age, gender, region). Instead it segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group.
- Segments can be:
  - **Underserved** — high opportunity scores, want more from existing products
  - **Overserved** — over-investing in outcomes that aren't critical; target for disruption
  - **Appropriately served** — satisfied; maintain current value

- **Agent rule**: When the user has collected outcomes with scores, help them identify outcome clusters that represent distinct market segments. This drives targeted innovation strategy.

---

### Stage 6: Formulate an Innovation Strategy

Based on the opportunity analysis, there are three strategic paths:

| Strategy | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Differentiated** | Improve existing products to address high-opportunity underserved outcomes |
| **Disruptive** | Create low-cost solutions for overserved segments that don't need all existing features |
| **New-Market** | Design products for a new job that is entirely unaddressed |

- **Agent rule**: When the opportunity landscape is clear (outcomes scored, segments identified), guide the user to select a strategy path and align their innovation roadmap accordingly.

---

### ⚠️ ODI Behavioral Guardrails for the Agent

These are absolute constraints the agent must respect:

| DO | DON'T |
|---|---|
| Always start by defining or confirming the Job-to-be-Done | Jump to solutions, features, or product ideas before the job is defined |
| Guide outcome statements with the correct format | Accept vague or solution-framed statements as valid outcomes |
| Compute opportunity scores when importance + satisfaction are available | Skip scoring or calculate it incorrectly |
| Reference the Universal Job Map when decomposing jobs | Invent arbitrary step structures disconnected from the 8 universal stages |
| Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments | Use demographics or assumptions to segment the market |
| Treat outcomes as stable, measurable success metrics | Confuse outcomes with features, preferences, or solutions |
| Call `get_odi_framework_guidelines` when stage guidance is needed | Guess at which stage comes next |

---

## 🛠 Technology Stack & Tools
- **Language**: Python 3.10+
- **MCP Framework**: `fastmcp` (Server and Client)
- **ASGI Server**: `uvicorn`
- **HTTP Client**: `httpx`
- **UI / Chat Client**: React + Vite (`apps/studio`), FastAPI sidecar (`apps/studio-api`)
- **LLM Client**: `openai` (OpenAI-compatible, used with Ollama locally)
- **Concurrency**: `asyncio`
- **Data Modeling / Validation**: `pydantic`

---

## 📄 README Maintenance Guardrail

`README.md` is the **primary human-facing entry point** for this project: a short,
high-level front door aimed at both users and developers. Detailed material lives
in `docs/` and is linked from the README. The agent MUST keep both current at all
times.

### When to update

Update the relevant file whenever any of the following change:

| Change type | Where to update |
|---|---|
| New or removed Python file / package | `README.md` **Code Overview** |
| New dependency added (`pip install ...`) | `README.md` **Quick Start → Prerequisites** |
| New way to run the project | `README.md` **Quick Start** and `docs/living-studio.md` |
| New MCP tool or capability | `README.md` **Code Overview** / relevant doc |
| New CLI command or flag | `docs/cli.md` |
| New connector kind | `docs/connectors.md` |
| New workflow or agent instruction | `docs/living-studio.md` |
| Deployment URL or cloud setup changes | `docs/deployment.md` |
| Roadmap item completed or added | `docs/roadmap.md` |
| Test layout or coverage changes | `docs/development.md` |

### Rules

- ✅ **Update docs in the same task** as the change that triggered it — never defer to a follow-up.
- ✅ **Keep README short**: it stays a high-level orientation page. Push detail into `docs/` and link to it rather than growing the README.
- ✅ **Keep the Quick Start accurate**: always reflect `uv run python scripts/dev.py` as the recommended launch command.
- ✅ **Keep Prerequisites up to date**: add any new `pip install` dependency immediately.
- ✅ **Mark Roadmap items `[x]` when completed** — do not leave stale unchecked items.
- ❌ **Never leave the README or `docs/` in a stale state** where documented commands or files no longer match the codebase.

---

## 🚧 Core Development Guardrails

### 1. Model Context Protocol (MCP) Implementation
- **Library Choice**: ALWAYS use [`fastmcp`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) for building the MCP architecture. Avoid using the lower-level Anthropic `mcp` SDK directly unless there is a hyper-specific edge case that `fastmcp` does not support.
- **Transport Protocol**: The project is currently prototyping with **HTTP transport** (not stdio). 
  - The server should be initialized using `mcp.run(transport="http", ...)`.
  - The client must connect to the HTTP endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
- **Tool Creation**: 
  - Register tools on the server using the `@mcp.tool` decorator.
  - **CRITICAL**: Provide comprehensive docstrings and strict Python type hints for every tool parameter. Explain exactly what the tool does and what data it expects, as this metadata is fed directly to the LLM for tool discovery.
  - **Contract Synchronization**: Whenever you add, modify, or remove an MCP tool in `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py`, you **MUST** simultaneously update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` (`ToolName`, `TOOL_SPECS`) and the `get_capabilities` return string. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` enforces the surface.

### 2. Async / Client Practices
- Use `asyncio` for client execution and IO-bound tool operations.
- Always use the `fastmcp.Client` securely within an asynchronous context manager (`async with client:`) to ensure connections are efficiently managed and closed.

### 3. Data Schema & Persistence (ODI Domain)
- Define all Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) entities (e.g., *Jobs*, *Steps*, *Desired Outcomes*, *Opportunity Scores*) using `pydantic` models.
- When expanding the server to accept complex payloads or to query data, utilize these Pydantic models for built-in type validation and schema enforcement before the server processes the request.

### 4. General Philosophy
- **Separation of Concerns**: Isolate the ODI data logic/retrieval from the MCP server tooling logic.
- **Agentic Purpose**: Remember that the tools being built are meant to be consumed by autonomous agents. Design tool interfaces that are intuitive for an LLM to call and interpret.
- **External connectors**: Integrations live in the `packages/connectors` workspace package. New kinds implement `agentic_odi_connectors.protocol.Connector` and register via `register_kind`. Do not write ingested records into `jobs_db` / outcomes unless a later mapping task says so.
- **MCP client vs ODI server**: The ODI FastMCP **server** exposes product tools. The MCP **client connector** uses `fastmcp.Client` over HTTP to ingest data from *external* MCP servers. Prefer in-memory `Client(server)` tests for that connector, same as server tests.

### 5. Testing Strategy (FastMCP)

#!/bin/sh
# SlayZone launcher for WSL2 / WSLg.
#
# `nix profile install github:debuglebowski/slayzone` installs the AppImage
# wrapped in a Nix FHS (bubblewrap) sandbox. That sandbox hides the host's
# /usr, which on WSLg breaks two things:
#
#   * fonts      - fontconfig resolves /etc/fonts -> /usr/share/fonts, which
#                  is empty inside the sandbox (text renders with no font)
#   * GPU        - Mesa's D3D12 driver lives in the host's /usr/lib/wsl/lib,
#                  so Electron's GPU process crash-loops and falls back to
#                  software rendering.
#
# So this launcher runs the AppImage (already extracted into the nix store by
# the flake) directly against the host, and supplies the four NSS/NSPR libs
# the AppImage expects (libnss3, libnspr4, libnssutil3, libsmime3), vendored
# from the Ubuntu .debs into ~/.local/share/slayzone/lib - no root needed.
#
# The store path is resolved from the nix profile, so `nix profile upgrade`
# keeps working.
set -e

# Resolve the extracted AppImage from the installed nix profile.
EXTRACTED=""
if command -v nix-store >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -e "$HOME/.nix-profile" ]; then
  EXTRACTED=$(nix-store --query --requisites "$(readlink -f "$HOME/.nix-profile")" 2>/dev/null |
    grep -E -- '-slayzone-[^/]*-extracted$' |
    head -n1)
fi
if [ -z "$EXTRACTED" ]; then
  for candidate in /nix/store/*-slayzone-*-extracted; do
    [ -d "$candidate" ] && EXTRACTED="$candidate"
  done
fi

if [ -z "$EXTRACTED" ] || [ ! -x "$EXTRACTED/AppRun" ]; then
  echo "slayzone: SlayZone not found in the nix profile." >&2
  echo "          Run: nix profile install --no-write-lock-file github:debuglebowski/slayzone" >&2
  exit 1
fi

VENDOR_LIB="$HOME/.local/share/slayzone/lib"
if [ -d "$VENDOR_LIB" ]; then
  LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$VENDOR_LIB${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH
fi

exec "$EXTRACTED/AppRun" "$@"

When the MCP server is asked to stop, it now closes its SQLite event store instead of dying with the connection still open — so the database is left clean, with no stray `-wal`/`-shm` files beside it.

Closes #122

---

## The problem

The MCP server opened a SQLite connection at import and never closed it. On `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` the process was killed outright, leaving the write-ahead log and shared-memory files on disk:

```
# before this change, after a SIGTERM:
old.db
old.db-shm      <- left behind
old.db-wal      <- left behind
```

Every write was already committed (`IntentStore.append` uses `with self.conn:`), so no data was being lost. But the connection was never closed, which means the WAL was never checkpointed and the sidecar files were left for the next process to recover. That is the state a crash or a `docker stop` leaves behind, and it is exactly the state the shutdown path should not be leaving behind.

## What a person experiences

You stop the server — `Ctrl+C`, `docker stop`, or `scripts/dev.py` shutting it down — and the database directory is left with a single `.db` file. No half-written WAL, no stale shared-memory segment, nothing for the next start to recover. The server still exits promptly (verified: **1 second** from SIGTERM to process exit), so nothing hangs.

## Specification

### The store can be flushed and closed

`IntentStore` gains a public `commit()` and an idempotent `close()`:

- `commit()` — flushes any open transaction. `append` already commits per event, so this is normally a no-op; it exists so the shutdown path can assert durability instead of assuming it.
- `close()` — commits, then closes the connection. Safe to call more than once, so two shutdown paths racing cannot raise `ProgrammingError`.

`Repository` (the protocol) gains `commit()` and `close()`:

| Implementation | `commit()` | `close()` |
|---|---|---|
| `SQLiteRepository` | delegates to the store | delegates to the store |
| `InMemoryRepository` | no-op | no-op |

### The server closes the store on the way out

Two paths, both landing on one idempotent `shutdown_store()`:

1. **A FastMCP lifespan hook.** This is the path that actually matters. Uvicorn handles `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` itself: it stops accepting connections, drains in-flight requests, then runs the ASGI lifespan shutdown. The hook runs there, so the store is closed *after* in-flight tool calls have finished — no request is ever cut off mid-write.

2. **Signal handlers.** `setup_graceful_shutdown()` installs handlers for `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` that flush the store and then **chain to the previous handler**, so the server's own shutdown behaviour is preserved rather than replaced. Uvicorn captures and restores the handlers it displaces, so the chain stays intact.

The handler is only a backstop: it guarantees the store is flushed even if the server is stopped by a path that does not run the lifespan.

## Verification

The behaviour is verified by running the real server and stopping it with `SIGTERM`:

```
# before (main):
old.db
old.db-shm
old.db-wal

# after (this branch):
new.db
```

The `-wal` and `-shm` files are gone, which is only possible if the connection was closed cleanly and the WAL was checkpointed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] SIGINT triggers the shutdown sequence without raising an exception
- [x] The store is committed and closed before the server exits
- [x] A test verifies `commit()` is called during shutdown
- [x] The process still exits promptly on SIGTERM (measured: 1s)
- [x] The store is closed exactly once, even if both shutdown paths fire
- [x] `uv run pytest` — 697 passed
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` — clean
- [x] `uv run mypy apps brand packages` — clean
- [x] `uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages` — clean

#!/bin/sh
SELF="$0"
while [ -L "$SELF" ]; do SELF=$(readlink "$SELF"); done
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SELF")" && pwd)"

NODE_MAJOR=$(node -e "process.stdout.write(process.versions.node.split('.')[0])" 2>/dev/null)
if [ -z "$NODE_MAJOR" ]; then
  echo "slay: node not found in PATH" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Production: slay.js is next to this script; dev: it's in ../dist/
if [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/slay.js" ]; then
  SLAY_JS="$SCRIPT_DIR/slay.js"
elif [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../dist/slay.js" ]; then
  SLAY_JS="$SCRIPT_DIR/../dist/slay.js"
else
  echo "slay: slay.js not found" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# node:sqlite needs --experimental-sqlite on Node 22; suppress ExperimentalWarning on all versions
if [ "$NODE_MAJOR" -le 22 ]; then
  exec node --experimental-sqlite --no-warnings "$SLAY_JS" "$@"
else
  exec node --no-warnings "$SLAY_JS" "$@"
fi

# Roadmap & Next Steps

As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:

- [x] **External MCP client connector**: Pluggable connectors package with an
  HTTP MCP ingest client, CLI adapter, and in-memory tests.
- [x] **Conversational rich surfaces**: the studio agent composes validated
  cards inline from a closed, client-owned catalog instead of describing them
  in prose.
- [x] **Map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts**: Turn connector records into
  jobs, outcomes, or evidence without mixing connector plumbing into the ODI
  store.
- [x] **First-run wizard**: A skippable, resumable four-step tour with inline
  connection repair, ending in the chosen surface or a handoff to the context
  conversation — isolated in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/` behind the
  `firstRunWizard` flag.
- [x] **Additional connector kinds**: REST/webhooks and similar integrations
  implementing the same `Connector` protocol.
- [x] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*,
  *Steps*, and *Outcomes*.
- [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `apps/cli` so the ODI dataset can be
  created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current
  MCP path.
- [x] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like
  `get_job_map(job_id)`, `get_outcomes(job_id)`, `get_step(step_id)`,
  `get_outcome(outcome_id)`, or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`.
- [x] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the FastMCP server to a lightweight
  SQLite repository containing actual user research data.
- [x] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the CLI chat up to an LLM (via the
  `openai` package) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently
  request customer insights when ideating features.

# Repository Architecture

Agentic ODI is a uv workspace with a single root `pyproject.toml` for shared tooling. Python distributions are imported by their stable `agentic_odi_*` package names; directory layout does not leak into imports.

## Layout

```text
apps/
  cli/            agentic_odi_cli         Typer CLI: local SQLite or remote MCP
  mcp-server/     agentic_odi_mcp_server  FastMCP server over HTTP
  studio-api/     agentic_odi_studio_api  FastAPI sidecar for the Studio SPA
  studio/         React + TypeScript + Vite SPA and Tauri 2 shell
packages/
  core/           agentic_odi_core        Domain, services, repositories, contract
  connectors/     agentic_odi_connectors  MCP client connectors and catalog
infra/cloudflare/ Worker + Wrangler config for the free-plan deployment
scripts/          Dev launcher, binary build, installer checks
tests/            Cross-package contract and launcher tests only
docs/             Architecture, reference material, Superpowers artifacts
packaging/        PyInstaller spec for the CLI binary
```

## Dependency Direction

```text
apps/cli ──────────────┐
apps/mcp-server ───────┼──▶ packages/core
apps/studio-api ───────┘         ▲
                                 │
apps/cli ──────────────▶ packages/connectors
```

- `packages/core` depends on no other workspace package.
- `packages/connectors` depends on `core` only where it needs shared models.
- Every runnable app may depend on `core`; none of them imports another app.
- The React SPA only talks to `apps/studio-api` over `/api`; it never calls MCP or the LLM directly.

## Persistence

- `SQLiteRepository` is the production default for the CLI, MCP server, and Studio API.
- The default database is `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_DB`.
- Studio conversation history and PM memory use a separate SQLite database,
  `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`, overridable with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`. They are
  sidecar-local and never enter the ODI repository or the MCP contract.
- `build_repository()` chooses SQLite by default and `InMemoryRepository` when `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:`, which is what tests use.
- The CLI selects its backend with `--backend local|mcp` or `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND`.
- The Studio API selects `local` (direct service calls) or `mcp` (passthrough) with `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` or `create_app(backend=...)`.

## MCP Contract

`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` owns `ToolName`, `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, and `TOOL_NAMES`. The live FastMCP registry is asserted against it by `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py`; the CLI's local handlers are checked by `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py`.

## Entry Points

| Command | Module |
|---|---|
| `agentic-odi` | `agentic_odi_cli.cli:app` |
| `agentic-odi-server` / `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | `agentic_odi_mcp_server.mcp_server:main` |
| `agentic-odi-studio-api` | `agentic_odi_studio_api.main:main` |
| `uv run python scripts/dev.py` | Dev launcher (MCP + Studio API) |

# Testing

## Commands

```bash
uv run pytest                       # all packages + root contract/launcher tests
uv run pytest packages/core         # one package
uv run pytest tests/contract        # MCP contract only
uv run mypy apps packages tests
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages
```

The root `pyproject.toml` owns pytest, coverage, ruff, mypy, and bandit configuration. There is no per-package test configuration to keep in sync.

## Layout

Tests live next to their package (`packages/*/tests`, `apps/*/tests`). Root `tests/` contains only cross-package checks:

- `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` — live FastMCP names, argument names, and required fields match `agentic_odi_core.contract.TOOL_SPECS`.
- `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py` — the CLI local-handler keys are a subset of `TOOL_NAMES`.
- `tests/scripts/` — dev launcher helpers and lifecycle.

## Isolation Rules

- Use `InMemoryRepository` in tests. `create_app(InMemoryRepository())` keeps the Studio API off the real `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`.
- The MCP server uses `build_repository()`; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` before import and call tools through `Client(mcp)` without HTTP.
- Async tests use `@pytest.mark.asyncio` (strict mode).

## Coverage

CI runs the root suite on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, collects coverage for every `agentic_odi_*` distribution, and uploads `coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job. Codecov requires 90% project coverage; patch coverage is advisory. Python tests and `apps/studio/**` are excluded from the report by `codecov.yml`.

## Frontend

npm --prefix apps/studio run lint
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run
npm --prefix apps/studio run build
cd apps/studio/src-tauri && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy -- -D warnings && cargo check
```

<task id="ses_e9718d66dffeg4ohm9Q2vyCJdf" state="completed">
<task_result>
Now I have a thorough understanding of the codebase. Here are my findings.

---

## 16 Concrete Developer Opportunities

Each opportunity was cross-referenced against the 30 open GitHub issues. Issues #123, #124, #122, #120, #119, #118, #117, #116, #114, #113, #110, #108, #107, #106, and #105 are **already tracked** — these 16 opportunities are new gaps **not** covered by any existing issue.

---

### 1. Studio API: add missing GET endpoints for jobs, steps, and outcomes

**Problem:** The Studio router has POST/PATCH/DELETE for `/jobs`, `/steps`, `/outcomes` but **no GET endpoints** to list or retrieve individual entities. The Studio frontend must use `fetch_canvas` (MCP HTTP calls) even when running in `local` backend mode, adding unnecessary network overhead.

**Files:** `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py` — only routes at lines 161-313 are POST/PATCH/DELETE; no `@router.get("/jobs")`, `@router.get("/jobs/{job_id}")`, or equivalent for steps/outcomes.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `GET /jobs` returns a list of all jobs
- `GET /jobs/{job_id}` returns a single job (404 if not found)
- Same pattern for `/steps` and `/outcomes`
- Respects MCP vs local backend (delegates to MCP when backend is "mcp")
- Follows existing `_as_http_error` error pattern

**Effort:** 2-3 hours

---

### 2. Studio API: add customer-outcomes and evidence endpoints

**Problem:** The router has zero routes for customer outcomes or evidence — no CRUD endpoints at all. The `schemas.py` file has no `CustomerOutcomeCreateRequest` or `EvidenceSchema`. The Studio frontend cannot manage customer outcomes or evidence through the API; it must fall back entirely to MCP passthrough.

**Files:** `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py` (lines 1-396 contain no customer-outcomes or evidence routes); `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/schemas.py` (no customer outcome/evidence schemas exist)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /customer-outcomes` endpoints
- `POST/GET/DELETE /evidence` endpoints
- Request/response schemas in `schemas.py`
- Consistent with existing job/step/outcome endpoint patterns

**Effort:** 3-4 hours

---

### 3. Studio API: `post_job`/`post_step`/`post_outcome` lack error handling

**Problem:** The POST routes for creating jobs, steps, and outcomes don't wrap service calls in `try/except`, while their PATCH/DELETE counterparts use `_as_http_error`. A `ValueOutOfRangeError` or `JobNotFoundError` from the service will produce a raw 500 Internal Server Error.

**Files:** `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:162-172` (post_job — no try/except), `:206-220` (post_step — no try/except), `:254-278` (post_outcome — no try/except). Compare with `patch_job` at `:185-189` which does wrap.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- All three POST routes wrap service calls in `try/except Exception`
- Domain errors are translated via `_as_http_error`
- Tests verify 400/404/422 responses (not 500) for invalid input

**Effort:** 45 minutes

---

### 4. LocalBackend missing `evaluate_outcome`, `get_odi_framework_guidelines`, `get_capabilities`

**Problem:** Three tools defined in `contract.py` and implemented in the MCP server are **not** in the LocalBackend's `_LOCAL_HANDLERS` dict. CLI users with `--backend local` cannot use these tools — calling them raises `NotImplementedError: "Unknown tool"`.

**Files:** `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:465-493` (`_LOCAL_HANDLERS` dict — missing `evaluate_outcome`, `get_odi_framework_guidelines`, `get_capabilities`). These exist in the MCP server at `mcp_server.py:252, 456-471` and in `contract.py:40, 43-44`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Add three handler methods to `LocalBackend` (delegating to `ODIService` or `core` functions)
- Add three entries to `_LOCAL_HANDLERS`
- Add CLI commands to `cli.py` (e.g., `odi evaluate`, `odi guidelines`, `odi capabilities`)
- Update `test_cli_contract.py` `LOCAL_TOOLS` set

**Effort:** 1-2 hours

---

### 5. No pagination on any list operation

**Problem:** Every list method across the Repository protocol, InMemoryRepository, and SQLiteRepository returns unbounded results. No `limit`/`offset` parameters exist in the interface, implementations, or tool specs. As the event store grows, list operations will become progressively slower.

**Files:** `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/repository.py:17-46` (Protocol — no pagination params), `:61-62, 104-105, 141-145, 172-175, 200-213` (InMemory — no pagination). `sqlite_repository.py:137-140, 195-198, 248-254, 304-309, 350-365` (SQLite — no pagination). `contract.py:55-139` (no pagination params in any `ToolSpec`).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Add optional `limit`/`offset` params to `list_jobs`, `list_customer_outcomes`, `list_evidence`, `get_outcomes`, `get_steps_for_job`
- Update both `Repository` Protocol and both implementations
- Add `limit`/`offset` to relevant `TOOL_SPECS` in `contract.py`
- Contract tests still pass

**Effort:** 3-4 hours

---

### 6. `InMemoryRepository` missing `reload()` method

**Problem:** `SQLiteRepository` has a `reload()` method (line 400-402) that re-reads the snapshot from the event store. `InMemoryRepository` has no equivalent. The `Repository` Protocol doesn't declare `reload`, so neither tests nor callers can rely on it existing. If `_LOCAL_HANDLERS` or any code calls `repo.reload()` on an `InMemoryRepository`, it will raise `AttributeError`.

**Files:** `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/sqlite_repository.py:400-402` (`reload` exists), `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/repository.py:49-226` (InMemory has no `reload`; only `clear()` at line 221). Protocol at `repository.py:10-47` doesn't declare `reload`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Add `reload()` to the `Repository` Protocol
- Implement `reload()` on `InMemoryRepository` (no-op or re-initialize from in-memory dicts)
- Test that both implementations have the method

**Effort:** 15 minutes

---

### 7. Extract shared `update_customer_outcome` field-merging logic

**Problem:** The exact same field-merging logic for updating customer outcomes (merging flat CLI/API args into nested `customer_value`/`business_value` dicts) is **duplicated** in two places. One is in the LocalBackend, the other in the MCP server. Both manually iterate over field lists and construct merged dicts. This should be a shared method in `ODIService`.

**Files:** `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:304-341` (LocalBackend `_update_customer_outcome` — manual field merge). `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:192-231` (`update_customer_outcome` tool — identical manual field merge). The shared helper should live in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/services.py:213-217` (existing `update_customer_outcome` method that just delegates to `repo.update_customer_outcome` without the merge logic).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Add a `apply_customer_outcome_updates(outcome_id, updates)` method to `ODIService` that handles the field merging
- Both LocalBackend and MCP server delegate to this method
- Contract tests and parity tests still pass

**Effort:** 2-3 hours

---

### 8. MCP `evaluate_outcome` error format is inconsistent

**Problem:** When `evaluate_outcome` can't find the job, it returns `json.dumps({..., "error": "Job not found: nope"})` (line 461). All other MCP tools return `"Error: ..."` string prefix or `"... not found: ..."` format. The CLI's `_parse_remote` at `backend.py:553` checks for `"Error:"` prefix or `" not found:"` substring. While the JSON string does contain " not found:" so it would be caught, the error message displayed to the user would be the raw JSON blob (e.g., `{"statement": ..., "valid": false, "job_id": "nope", "error": "Job not found: nope"}`), not a clean message.

**Files:** `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:457-471` (inconsistent error return). `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:550-564` (`_parse_remote` error detection).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `evaluate_outcome` returns `"Error: Job not found: nope"` (consistent with other tools) when the job doesn't exist
- When valid and job exists, returns the JSON result as before
- Test verifies error is caught by `_parse_remote` and raised as `BackendError`

**Effort:** 15 minutes

---

### 9. MCP server `main()` hardcodes port 8000

**Problem:** The server's `main()` function calls `mcp.run(transport="http", port=8000)` with no way to override the port. In development environments or when running multiple instances, users cannot configure an alternate port.

**Files:** `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:479-480`

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Support `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_PORT` environment variable (default: 8000)
- Support `--port` CLI flag via `if __name__ == "__main__"`
- Tests verify default and custom port resolution

**Effort:** 15 minutes

---

### 10. Studio API `/capabilities` endpoint returns backend type instead of capabilities

**Problem:** The capabilities endpoint returns `{"capabilities": app.state.backend}`, which is the literal string `"local"` or `"mcp"`. This does not communicate what the server can actually do. Users calling this endpoint expect the `CAPABILITIES` markdown string (defined in `messages.py:50-61`) or a structured list of available features.

**Files:** `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/app.py:70-72`. `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/messages.py:50-61` (the `CAPABILITIES` constant).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `/capabilities` returns `{"capabilities": CAPABILITIES}` (the markdown string from core)
- Response is useful for clients deciding which UI to render

**Effort:** 10 minutes

---

### 11. Studio API chat endpoint has no error handling

**Problem:** The `post_chat` endpoint (line 390-396) wraps `stream_chat(...)` in a `StreamingResponse` with no `try/except`. If the MCP server is unreachable, the LLM call fails, or the memory service raises an exception, the SSE stream will break mid-response or return an unhandled exception instead of a structured error event.

**Files:** `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:390-396`. `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py` (the `stream_chat` function).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Catch exceptions during stream generation and return an SSE `error` event with a descriptive message
- Return HTTP 502 if the MCP server is unreachable
- Tests verify error events are emitted as SSE, not raw 500s

**Effort:** 1-2 hours

---

### 12. Studio API `post_step`/`post_outcome` return JSON strings while `post_job` returns a dict

**Problem:** The three POST endpoints return inconsistent result types from their `"result"` field:
- `post_job` (line 172): `job.model_dump(mode="json")` — returns a **dict**
- `post_step` (line 218): `.model_dump_json()` — returns a **JSON string**
- `post_outcome` (line 276): `.model_dump_json()` — returns a **JSON string**

The Studio frontend cannot reliably parse the `"result"` field without knowing which endpoint was called.

**Files:** `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:162-172` (post_job — dict result), `:206-220` (post_step — string result), `:254-278` (post_outcome — string result).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- All three POST endpoints use `.model_dump(mode="json")` for the `"result"` field
- Response shape is consistent across all create endpoints
- Tests verify `result` is a dict in all three responses

**Effort:** 20 minutes

---

### 13. No unit tests for `evaluate_outcome_statement`

**Problem:** The `evaluate_outcome_statement` function (`evaluation.py:20-64`) validates outcome statement format — checking direction prefix (Minimize/Maximize), presence of "the", context markers (when/while/before/after/during/if/as), word count minimum, character length maximum, and vague terms. Despite being 45 lines of branching logic, it has **zero test coverage**.

**Files:** `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/evaluation.py:20-64` (no tests exist). The only test file touching evaluation is `test_odi.py` in the MCP server, which only tests `evaluate_outcome` as a full MCP tool (and that test asserts the JSON result contains `"id"` for a job, not the evaluation logic).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Test valid statement passes all checks (valid=true, no issues)
- Test missing direction prefix → issue added
- Test missing "the" → issue added
- Test missing context marker → issue added
- Test too-short statement (<4 words) → issue added
- Test vague terms detected (better/improve/optimize/faster/easier) → issue added
- Test statement >200 chars → issue added

**Effort:** 1-2 hours

---

### 14. No MCP-level tests for `evaluate_outcome` and `promote_evidence` tools

**Problem:** The MCP server implements `evaluate_outcome` (line 456-471) and `promote_evidence` (line 420-453), but no tests exercise these through the MCP client interface. The `test_parity.py` tests step/outcome CRUD and customer outcome updates, but omits `evaluate_outcome` entirely. The `promote_evidence` tool is only tested through the CLI's `test_connectors_cli.py:394-457`, which tests the CLI wrapper, not the MCP tool's error handling paths.

**Files:** `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_parity.py` (lines 1-112 — tests step/outcome CRUD and customer outcome updates, no `evaluate_outcome` or `promote_evidence`). `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_odi.py` (lines 1-92 — tests basic workflow and `get_capabilities`, no `evaluate_outcome` or `promote_evidence`). `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:420-453` (untested error paths in `promote_evidence`).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Test `evaluate_outcome` with a valid statement
- Test `evaluate_outcome` with an invalid job_id (error path)
- Test `promote_evidence` error path for non-existent evidence_id
- Test `promote_evidence` error path for unknown target

**Effort:** 1-2 hours

---

### 15. CLI `connectors list` command lacks `--json` flag

**Problem:** The `connectors list` command (`connectors.py:114-125`) only outputs tab-separated text. Unlike every other entity command in the CLI (jobs, steps, outcomes, evidence, customer outcomes all support `--json`), the connectors list command has no machine-readable output option. The `catalog` subcommand has `--json` (line 131) but `list` doesn't.

**Files:** `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/connectors.py:114-125` (no `--json` option). Compare with `desired_outcomes.py:19` and `customer_outcomes.py` (both have `JSON_OPTION`).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Add `--json` flag to `connectors list` command
- When `--json` is passed, output a JSON array of connector configs with name, kind, url, enabled fields
- Human-readable output is unchanged

**Effort:** 30 minutes

---

### 16. MCP `_extract_json` is fragile for mixed response formats

**Problem:** The `_extract_json` function (`backend.py:567-574`) finds the first `{` or `[` character in a response string and parses from there. This is fragile because: (1) some MCP tools return human-readable text before the JSON (e.g., `"Customer outcome created successfully: {...}"`), and (2) error messages could contain `{` characters before the actual JSON payload. The function also doesn't handle the case where `text.find("{")` returns a position inside an error message.

**Files:** `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:567-574` (`_extract_json`). `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:550-564` (`_parse_remote` uses `_extract_json`). `test_backend_edges.py:178-188` only tests simple cases.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Add test: response with `{` in error text before JSON payload is parsed correctly
- Add test: response with nested `{` in an outer JSON wrapper is parsed correctly
- If simple fix isn't possible, add a `# TODO` with explanation of the limitation

**Effort:** 1 hour

---

## Summary of Analysis

**Read-only research complete.** I examined the full Python codebase: `packages/core` (domain models, services, SQLite event-sourced repository, contract, errors, evaluation, schema), `packages/connectors` (MCP/REST connectors, registry, factory, catalog, sink, mapping), `apps/cli` (backend, CLI commands, connectors adapter), `apps/mcp-server` (FastMCP server with all tool handlers), `apps/studio-api` (FastAPI router, schemas, memory, MCP data, probes), and all test files.

**Key architectural findings:**
- The `Repository` Protocol and `InMemoryRepository` are in `repository.py` — the SQLite repo is event-sourced over `IntentStore` (append-only events + in-memory snapshot)
- The MCP server returns string responses (JSON strings, "Error:" prefixes, "created successfully: ..." wrappers) — the CLI's `_parse_remote` must reverse-engineer the format
- The Studio API supports both local and MCP backends, but has incomplete endpoint coverage (no GET routes, no customer-outcomes/evidence routes)
- The contract layer (`contract.py`) defines `ToolName` enum and `TOOL_SPECS` — contract tests assert MCP tools and CLI handlers match this
- Recent commit #128 added a comprehensive error hierarchy (`errors.py`) — all domain errors now inherit from `OdiError`
- Issues #105 (--version), #106 (compute_opportunity_score tests), #113 (connectors health), #116 (Job validation), #118 (data export), #123 (interactive wizard), #124 (connector config validation) are **already addressed** or in progress — I excluded these from the 16
</task_result>
</task>

I now have research from four parallel agents. I have 18 + 16 + 11 + ~10 = ~55 candidate opportunities. After deduplication against the ~20 existing slayzone tasks and the GitHub issues list, and merging the overlapping ones, I have 50 distinct, high-value, junior-implementable issues ready.

Here is my plan — **the deliverables and workflow only, no execution**. I will not make any edits or changes to the system.

## Plan

### What I'll produce
A single read-only inspection result: **50 ready-to-file SlayZone backlog issues**, each with:
- A short, outcome-focused title
- A concise description answering *why* it matters (the Steve Jobs "what a person experiences" angle)
- A **prompt** block a human (or junior agent) can execute verbatim
- Acceptance criteria
- File/line references
- Rough effort (all ≤4h)
- A tag (frontend / backend / docs / cli / mcp / infra / tests) and priority

The 50 are drawn from the agent analyses above, deduplicated against the 20 issues already open on GitHub and the existing slayzone tasks (`agentic-odi` project currently has only 2 tasks: the mascot task and a "Create backlog" task), and grouped roughly as: ~12 Studio/UX polish, ~12 backend/CLI/MCP/data, ~10 infrastructure/docs/CI/release, ~8 test-coverage gaps, ~8 cross-cutting/duplicate-removal items.

### How they get into SlayZone
I verified the SlayZone CLI surface (`slay tasks create --title <t> --description <d> --status backlog --project agentic-odi`). I'll create them in a batch via a bash loop calling `slay tasks create`, then `slay tasks list --json` to confirm exactly 52 tasks exist (2 existing + 50 new) and that all carry `status: backlog`. Each issue's `prompt` lives as the trailing section of its `description` so a human can `slay tasks view <id>` and copy it.

### Order of work (in plan mode nothing actually runs)
1. Emit the 50 issue specs as a `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-23-slayzone-50-issues-plan.md` design document (read-only; not created in this read-only phase).
2. In execution mode: run the `slay tasks create` batch.
3. Verify with `slay tasks list --json` (count = 52, all `backlog`).

### Conflicts avoided
I cross-checked every candidate against the 15 open PRs and ~20 open issues. For example I will **not** re-file anything that already has a tracking branch (issue-91, issue-119, issue-122, #84 capability-manifest/#125, etc.). Where an existing issue is oversized (e.g. #82 "no surface may lie", #81 "must survive you", #86 "PR must not be able to lie"), I split it into a small verifiable first increment rather than the whole epic, so each stays under the 4h cap.

### Open questions for you (Steve Jobs hat on)

// Reads: none. Writes: none on disk (only calls `slay tasks create`).
import { execFileSync } from "child_process";
import { existsSync, readdirSync } from "fs";

let EXTRACTED = "";
try {
  const pf = execFileSync("readlink", ["-f", process.env.HOME + "/.nix-profile"]).toString().trim();
  const reqs = execFileSync("nix-store", ["--query", "--requisites", pf]).toString().split(/\n/);
  const m = reqs.find((l) => /-slayzone-[^/]*-extracted$/.test(l));
  if (m && existsSync(m + "/AppRun")) EXTRACTED = m;

}

## Framing the problem you described

Most current tasks read as "docs says mypy, fix mypy line," "add a toggle," "fix a tool name in a template" — they reduce maintainer friction but don't change what a user *feels* when using Agentic ODI. The ones that should outrank are the ones that turn a **friction moment** into a **delight moment** — the Steve Jobs standard from your earlier ask.

## My proposed filter (your call)
I'd re-scope each task through a **User Outcome > Implementation Detail** frame:
- **Bad:** "Fix `odi_schema` in `_mcp_reference.html`" → sounds noise.

I have all 83 backlog items (batch 1's stragglers + the 50 second-batch). I've read them and their full descriptions. Here is the grooming plan.

## Grooming plan for the 83 backlog tasks

**Frame applied:** every task gets a *user-outcome headline* (what a person feels/experiences), a *Why*, *Acceptance = the delight*, and the *technical breakdown preserved verbatim* under a collapsible `# Implementation (for the implementer agent)` section. Atomic, ≤4h, no two tasks delivering the same outcome. Per your "merge if helpful" note, I'll collapse the **~7 pure-docs-nit** tasks (mypy lines, wrangler path, Streamlit note, stale index.html, version-sync, schema toolname) into one user-facing task to kill the noise.

### What counts as "noise → joy" examples (the pattern I'll apply to all 83)

| Old (noise) | Groomed user-outcome title | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Fix mypy target docs in docs/development.md | **A contributor's first install + test run works first time** | Wrong mypy target in the guide = 15 min wasted. One-line fix → no papercut. |
| Fix odi_schema tool name in generated MCP reference | **Docs show tools that actually exist, so pasting a name works** | A wrong tool name is a silent failure. Correct = no friction. |
| Sync pyproject.toml version with releases | **odi --version tells the truth** | 12 releases in but it prints 0.1.0 — trust dies in 3s. |
| Remove stale unused website/index.html | **The repo doesn't ship a ghost file** | Stale index.html = confusion about which docs are live. Delete it. |
| Wire read_cli() into site build or correct the README claim | **The CLI reference on the site matches the real CLI** | Docs that "cannot drift" but do = broken promise. Make it true or say so. |

### Group 1 — Studio / UX joy (21 tasks)
These become *behavioral* titles (the current batch 2 UX set is mostly fine; just re-led with outcome).
- "Add a dark-mode toggle persisted to user settings" → **Switch to dark mode and have it stick across tabs / restarts** — *Why:* forcing dark is fine, forcing it with no light option is a wall.
- "Export the current thread to a Markdown transcript" → **Take any studio conversation and paste-ready it into a doc**
- "Per-step Skip on the first-run tour" → **Skip a tour step without abandoning the whole walkthrough**
- "Show an unread-count badge on the CatchUp (bell) button" → **Know there's something waiting without opening the bell** (and I'll **merge** the ChangelogModal mark-read test + bell badge into one task: "Catch-up is reliable: counts + read-state stay correct" — they're the same outcome.)
- "Save as opportunity thesis from the landscape" → **Turn a scored outcome into a shareable thesis card in one click**
- "Label seed/demo outcomes as Sample data" → **Never mistake a bundled sample outcome for your own work**
- "Add a recovery action to UnknownNode surface" → **When a surface can't render, copy the raw spec and recover** — *merge: I'll **merge this with "Promote evidence→outcome Studio form"**? No — distinct outcomes; keep separate.

### Group 2 — Backend / CLI / MCP truth (28 tasks)
The "contract truth" cluster — every one becomes "does what it says on the tin."
- "Enforce ODI outcome-statement format at write time" → **Bad outcome statements are refused at the door with a fix hint** (not silently stored and mis-scored later)
- "Validate job-map step order within 1-8" → **A job step can't be placed in a non-existent Ulwick phase**
- "Sort get_outcomes by opportunity score desc by default" → **The outcomes most worth solving float to the top automatically**
- "odi summary <job_id>" → **One command reads back a job like a person would brief a teammate**
- "Backend auto with local→mcp fallback" → **The CLI keeps working when the sidecar is down, and tells you**
- "Make MCP evaluate_outcome return a consistent error string" + "Harden _extract_json parsing" → **Merge into one:** "MCP errors read like errors to humans (and to the CLI), not JSON blobs"
- "Make MCP server port configurable" → **Run two MCP servers without port fights**
- "MCP streaming progress events" → **Long tools stop the spinner and say what they're doing**
- "Return CAPABILITIES from /capabilities" → **/capabilities describes what it can do, not a label**
- "Add error handling to chat SSE stream" → **Chat failures show a clear message, not a dead stream**
- "Normalize POST result to a dict" → **Every create endpoint returns the same shape so clients don't special-case**
- "Implement missing LocalBackend handlers" → **odi works offline the same set of tools as online**
- "Add pagination to Repository list methods" → **Jobs/steps/outcomes lists stay fast and paged at 10k rows too**
- "Implement reload() on InMemoryRepository" → **Tests and the snapshot reload speak the same interface**
- "Wrap Studio API POST handlers in error handling" → **A bad payload returns 400, not a 500 that says nothing**
- "Publish OpenAPI schema" → **The sidecar has a contract the Studio and external tools can rely on**
- "Add --dry-run to connector ingest" → **Preview an ingest before it touches your outcomes**
- "Cache REST connector health" → **connector health is instant for things checked moments ago**

Grooming complete. Here's what I did.

## What shipped
Rewrote and tagged every task **still in the `backlog` column** (47 of 52 — the live agent had advanced 5 others into `done`/`in_progress` while I worked, and per your rule I stopped touching those). Each groomed task now reads:

- **Title = a user-outcome headline** (e.g. *"Bad outcome statements are refused at the door with a fix hint"*) instead of an implementation verb
- **`## Why (user outcome)`** → **`## What good looks like (acceptance)`** → **`## Implementation (verbatim technical spec)`** (files, flags, test command) → **`## Theme`**
- **A `theme:…` tag** so the backlog clusters into roadmap increments, with 10 theme tags created for the project (each distinct color).

## The clusters (roadmap increments)
| Theme tag | Count | Value increment |
|---|---|---|
| `studio-joy` | 14 | The Studio stops the little lies: no silent successes, no fake data, keyboard-first, no dead-ends |
| `docs-truth` | 6 | Docs match the code; first contributor run works first time |
| `cli-robust` | 6 | CLI is scriptable, resilient to a down sidecar, and can export/summarize/paginate |
| `ship-reliable` | 5 | Verifiable releases, OpenAPI contract, CI gates, recorded ADRs |
| `docs-site` | 5 | The docs site becomes a real docs site (search, dark, copy, anchors, catalog) |
| `tests` | 4 | Guardrails that prevent specific regressions (scores, formats, contract parity) |
| `catch-up`, `reliability`, `parity`, `trust-data` | 2–1 each | Bell/unread truth, no locked-DB, offline==online, ODI-data integrity |

## Two notes
1. **The 5 moved tasks** (mostly first-batch docs-nits: version sync, wrangler path, mypy docs, etc.) were left untouched in their new stage — they're already being closed out by the live agent.
2. **Titles were rewritten in place** via `slay tasks update` — so any external references by ID are intact, but if anything linked to the *old title strings*, those won't match any more. If you need, I can emit a title crosswalk.

Want me to (a) also groom the 3 pre-existing inbox meta-tasks ("PR Agent", "Create backlog", etc.) the same way, or (b) start implementing the highest-value cluster (`studio-joy` or `trust-data`) next?
